name: WPLifeCycle – Free PHP Version Info & Website Manager
author: Funlus Oy

sections.description:
WPLifeCycle connects a WordPress website to centralized monitoring and management while keeping each site protected by its own token-based connection. It combines lifecycle visibility, operational tools, security controls, and recovery workflows in one plugin.

Key features

  • Lifecycle monitoring for PHP, WordPress, MySQL, and installed plugins
  • Token-based WPLifeCycle connection with automatic and on-demand telemetry updates
  • Security scanning and hardening with OWASP checks, XML-RPC control, custom login URLs, login attempt limits, login honeypots, new administrator cooldowns, and IP allowlists and blocklists
  • Security events and access logs with super critical incident monitoring and tamper-evident event chains
  • Performance and SEO scans with actionable scores and findings
  • Plugin and hook monitoring for update availability, history, registered actions, filters, and conflicts
  • One-click and scheduled updates for WordPress core, plugins, and themes
  • Integrated backups and restores with integrity checks, safe archive handling, remote storage support, scheduling, and retention controls
  • Standalone WordPress migration for restoring a compatible backup into a clean WordPress installation
  • Secure admin links that are HTTPS-only, single-use, and time-limited

Built for real-world maintenance workflows with consent-based data sharing, minimal setup, server-conscious scans, and translation support.

Usage

  • Open Tools → WPLifeCycle to view PHP version details and run scans.
  • Click Generate Secure Admin Link to create a one-off login URL.
  • Grant data-sharing consent if you want this site monitored centrally.

Video
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install via Plugins → Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. (Optional) Go to Settings → WPLifeCycle and enter the one-time connection code from WPLifeCycle.
sections.faq:
Can I use it in my language?

Yes. Translate the included .po file with your preferred editor and drop the resulting .mo back into the plugin’s languages folder.
